name: Regexp over String
description: What a String does when a pattern is handed to it — searching, splitting, substituting, and rewriting in place.

scenarios.title: Matching a String answers a match with its captures
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code matches a String against a pattern with groups
scenarios.then: it answers a match carrying those captures

scenarios.title: Global substitution replaces every occurrence
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes globally with a replacement String
scenarios.then: every match is replaced

scenarios.title: A block decides each global replacement
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes globally with a block
scenarios.then: each match is replaced by that iteration's block result

scenarios.title: Single substitution replaces only the first
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes once with a replacement String
scenarios.then: only the first match is replaced

scenarios.title: Scanning a group-less pattern collects the matches
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code scans with a pattern carrying no groups
scenarios.then: it collects each matched substring

scenarios.title: Scanning a pattern with groups collects them per match
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code scans with a pattern carrying groups
scenarios.then: it collects one group list per match

scenarios.title: Splitting divides on each match
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits a String on a pattern
scenarios.then: it answers the fields between the matches

scenarios.title: A capturing group in the separator becomes a field
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits on a pattern carrying a group
scenarios.then: each captured substring is interleaved among the fields

scenarios.title: A positive limit stops splitting and keeps the rest whole
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits with a positive limit
scenarios.then: the remainder stays as the last field

scenarios.title: A negative limit keeps the trailing empty fields
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits with a negative limit on a String ending in separators
scenarios.then: the trailing empty fields are kept

scenarios.title: Searching a String answers a byte offset
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code searches a String for a pattern
scenarios.then: it answers the byte offset of the first match

scenarios.title: Searching can start from a position
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code searches for a pattern from a byte position
scenarios.then: it answers the first match at or after that position

scenarios.title: A negative search position counts from the end
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code searches for a pattern from a negative position
scenarios.then: the search starts that far back from the end

scenarios.title: A search that finds nothing from there answers nothing
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code searches from a position past every occurrence
scenarios.then: it answers nothing

scenarios.title: A position inside a character snaps to that character's start
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code searches from a byte position inside a multibyte character
scenarios.then: the search starts at that character's boundary

scenarios.title: Slicing by a pattern answers what matched
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code slices a String with a pattern
scenarios.then: it answers the matched substring

scenarios.title: Slicing by a pattern and a group answers that capture
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code slices a String with a pattern and a group index
scenarios.then: it answers that capture

scenarios.title: A block decides the single replacement too
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes once with a block
scenarios.then: the first match is replaced by the block's result

scenarios.title: Scanning with a block hands each match over
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code scans with a block
scenarios.then: the block receives each match in turn

scenarios.title: Splitting on a String is still the ordinary split
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits a String on another String
scenarios.then: it answers what the language's own split answers

scenarios.title: Splitting drops a group that did not take part
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits on a pattern whose optional group did not match
scenarios.then: no empty placeholder appears among the fields

scenarios.title: Scanning keeps the same group as nothing
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code scans with a pattern whose optional group did not match
scenarios.then: that position in the group list holds nothing

scenarios.title: A zero-width separator does not open with an empty field
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits a String on a zero-width pattern
scenarios.then: the fields are its characters with no leading empty one

scenarios.title: A zero-width split counts real splits against the limit
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits on a zero-width pattern with a positive limit
scenarios.then: it stops after that many splits and keeps the remainder

scenarios.title: An empty field between two separators is a field
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code splits a String holding two adjacent separators
scenarios.then: the empty field between them is kept

scenarios.title: A numbered backreference in the replacement expands
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes globally with a replacement naming a group by number
scenarios.then: each replacement carries that group's capture

scenarios.title: A named backreference expands too
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes globally with a replacement naming a group by name
scenarios.then: each replacement carries that group's capture

scenarios.title: Single substitution expands them as well
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes once with a replacement carrying a backreference
scenarios.then: the replacement carries that group's capture

scenarios.title: A Hash replacement looks each whole match up
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes globally with a Hash replacement
scenarios.then: each match is replaced by the value it maps to

scenarios.title: An escape nobody defined stays as it was written
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes with a replacement carrying an unrecognised escape
scenarios.then: it appears as its two literal characters

scenarios.title: A named backreference to a group that does not exist is an error
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes with a replacement naming a capture the pattern does not declare
scenarios.then: an index error is raised

scenarios.title: A malformed named backreference is a pattern error
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes with a replacement whose name marker carries no name
scenarios.then: a pattern error is raised

scenarios.title: The zeroth backreference is the whole match
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes with a replacement naming group zero
scenarios.then: each replacement carries the whole match

scenarios.title: A replacement argument outranks a block
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes globally with both a replacement String and a block
scenarios.then: the replacement String is used

scenarios.title: Assigning through a pattern overwrites what matched
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code assigns into a String through a pattern
scenarios.then: the matched region is replaced in place

scenarios.title: Assigning through a pattern and a group overwrites that group
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code assigns into a String through a pattern and a group index
scenarios.then: that group's region is replaced in place

scenarios.title: Assigning through a String is still the ordinary assignment
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code assigns into a String through another String
scenarios.then: it behaves as the language's own assignment does

scenarios.title: Assigning through indices is too
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code assigns into a String through Integer arguments
scenarios.then: it behaves as the language's own assignment does

scenarios.title: Assigning through a pattern that does not match is an error
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code assigns into a String through a pattern that does not occur
scenarios.then: an index error is raised

scenarios.title: Cutting by a pattern answers what was cut and removes it
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code cuts a match out of a String
scenarios.then: it answers the matched substring and the String no longer holds it

scenarios.title: Cutting a pattern that does not match changes nothing
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code cuts by a pattern that does not occur
scenarios.then: it answers nothing and the String is unchanged

scenarios.title: Cutting leaves the last match as its own
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads the last match after cutting by a pattern
scenarios.then: it holds the cut's own match

scenarios.title: Cutting by an index is still the ordinary cut
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code cuts a String by an Integer index
scenarios.then: that character is removed

scenarios.title: Cutting by a start and a length is too
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code cuts a String by an Integer start and length
scenarios.then: that range is removed

scenarios.title: And cutting by a String
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code cuts a String by another String
scenarios.then: its first occurrence is removed

scenarios.title: A raise inside a scan block reaches the caller
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code scans with a block that raises and rescues around the call
scenarios.then: the block's exception is what it rescues

scenarios.title: A raise inside a substitution block reaches the caller too
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes with a block that raises and rescues around the call
scenarios.then: the block's exception is what it rescues

scenarios.title: Global substitution with nothing to substitute asks for an enumerator
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes globally with neither a block nor a replacement
scenarios.then: the invocation fails naming the enumerator it could not build

scenarios.title: Single substitution with nothing to substitute is an error
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code substitutes once with neither a block nor a replacement
scenarios.then: an argument error is raised

text: A String handed a pattern searches, splits, substitutes or rewrites itself.
Each of those takes the same pattern and answers differently, so each is
witnessed separately, and where a String argument reaches the same method
the scenario says the ordinary behavior still stands — the pattern surface
layers over the language's own rather than replacing it.
Splitting and scanning disagree deliberately about a group that did not
take part: splitting drops it, scanning keeps the hole. Both are witnessed
on the same pattern, because the contrast is the contract.
Replacement text is a small language of its own, so its scenarios cover what
expands, what stays literal, and what is refused — a name no group carries,
and a name marker with no name behind it.
